name: ParseDocument
title: Parse Document
description: Read a file into its structure. Text in order, tables as rows, figures, lists, dates, and where each sits on the page
whenToUse: Read a document you already hold into a structure a pipeline or an Agent can work with: the text in reading order, every table as header and rows with numbers and units parsed, every figure as an image with its caption, every ordered list with its steps, the dates the document carries and where it was found, and for each of those the page and box it came from. Best when something downstream needs the TABLES or the FIGURES as things of their own rather than prose, or needs to point back at the exact place a figure came from. It only reads a file that already exists, on the platform's own service, and never sends the file to a third party.

inputs.name: file
inputs.description: The file: { downloadUrl, key, etag } as S3 File Content emits, or any object with a URL

outputs.name: document
outputs.description: title, pages, kind, scanned, dates found with where, the file's metadata, content hash, parser version

outputs.name: text
outputs.description: The whole document as markdown in reading order, headings kept; a PDF's page by page, each opened by its own page number as <!-- page n -->

outputs.name: sections
outputs.description: The heading tree, each with level, page range, and the ids of the tables and figures inside it

outputs.name: tables
outputs.description: Every table, header and rows as written, cells parsed to numbers and units, the tidy form when clean, with page and box

outputs.name: figures
outputs.description: Every figure with its caption, a PNG (base64) rendered from the page, and its page and box

outputs.name: lists
outputs.description: Every ordered list, steps included, each item with its number, text, depth, page and box

outputs.name: review
outputs.description: Regions worth a vision read, each rendered from the page: tables that failed a check, then charts, capped per document (docs/unoverse/data/documents/review.md)

outputs.name: quality
outputs.description: OCR and table confidence, text density, warnings that say "distrust this"

outputs.name: firstPages
outputs.description: The first two pages of the text, cut at the third page's mark (a file with no pages at 8000 characters), for a read that names the document without its whole text

outputs.name: outline
outputs.description: Every heading in order, each { id, page, title, firstWords }: what the document holds, for a read that names its sections

outputs.name: parts
outputs.description: The tables and the meaningful figures, shaped as parts: { tables: [{ partId, title, caption, description, page, box, columns, rowCount, firstRows, stitchedFrom, checks, rowsFile, pictureFile }], figures: [{ partId, title, caption, description, kind, page, box, pictureFile }] }

outputs.name: files
outputs.description: What to save of this reading, by name, never where: [{ name, contentType, text | base64 }], the text, the structure, each table's rows and each picture. A save step puts them where the caller keeps them

fileUrl.title: File URL
fileUrl.description: A URL the service can fetch the file from, usually a presigned link wired from an upstream file node, e.g. return signal.file.downloadUrl

fileName.title: File Name
fileName.description: The name with its extension, e.g. memorandum.pdf. The kind is read from the bytes, the name is for the filename dates and a better title.

includeFigures.title: Include figures
includeFigures.description: Render every figure as a PNG into the reply. Off for a text-and-tables read, which is smaller and faster.

ocr.title: OCR scanned pages
ocr.description: Run OCR on pages with no text layer. Off to read only what the file already says.

authRequired.title: Require sign-in
authRequired.description: Only a signed-in caller may run this step. Leave off and it runs for whoever the workflow's trigger admitted, which is the usual answer.

authRole.title: Require role
authRole.description: A claim the caller's account must carry, as noun:verb (finance:approve, payments:refund). Leave blank to require only that they are signed in.

package.name: documents
package.packageFile:
# DOCUMENTS — the platform's own document service (services/documents, a Python service beside
# umap): a file in, its structure out. Text in reading order, every table as rows, every figure
# as an image with its caption, every ordered list, the dates a document carries, and where on
# which page each sits. docs/unoverse/data/documents/README.md.
#
# ONE DOOR, ONE NODE: ParseDocument, RenderDocument, InventoryFolder, ReadCover, ReadValues. Each is a JOB on
# the service (start, poll, collect), which is the LlamaParse shape, so the poll capability does
# the waiting. A door does one job, so one can be improved or replaced without touching what
# calls it: a census before reading, a cover before filing, a parse when the whole is wanted.
#
# THE HOST IS THE ENGINE, at loopback (`scope.engineUrl`, :4101), which forwards to the service
# (routes/documents.ts) the way it reaches umap. A node's call must be https or loopback
# (allowedHosts.ts refuses a plaintext request to any other host), and a compose service on the
# Docker network is neither; the engine holds the service's address so no node and no file does.

name: documents
displayName: Documents
description: >-
  Read a file into its structure with the platform's document service. Text, tables as rows,
  figures, lists, dates, provenance
version: 0.1.0
category: ingest
logoUrl: https://res.cloudinary.com/sonik/image/upload/v1751366180/gravity/icons/gravityIcon.png

features:
  - Parse PDF, Word, slides, spreadsheets, HTML and images into one typed structure
  - Tables as rows with units parsed, figures as images, ordered lists as steps
  - Render any page or region as an image
  - "Inventory a folder: kinds, pages, dates, duplicates"
  - "Read a cover: what each file is about and the date it states, from named cells, no model"
  - "Read values: the figures a parsed document stated, refused whole when they do not add up to what it says about itself"

allowedHosts:
  # LOOPBACK ONLY, numeric form (the pattern rejects a bare "localhost"): every call goes to the
  # engine's own listener, which forwards to the service. No third-party host, ever.
  - 127.0.0.1

requires:
  executorVersion: ">=1.6.0"
  transport: [json]
  # Every door is a job: without `poll` an executor would settle on the receipt and emit the job
  # id as the answer.
  poll: true

files.api/run.yaml:
# ONE JOB ON THE PLATFORM'S OWN DOCUMENT SERVICE, through the engine at loopback (package.yaml
# says why). POST starts it and answers { id, status: PENDING }; the poll asks the job until it is
# COMPLETED or FAILED; the finished reply carries the structure under `result`.

- name: job
  method: POST
  url: "return scope.engineUrl + '/documents/parse'"
  transport: json

  body:
    file_url: "{{ config.fileUrl }}"
    file_name: "return String(config.fileName || '').trim() || undefined"
    include_figures: "return config.includeFigures !== false"
    ocr: "return config.ocr !== false"

  timeoutMs: 60000

  # The service answers a refusal as { detail } (FastAPI's convention) or { error } (the engine's
  # forward when it cannot reach the service). Neither is a job.
  error:
    when: "return !!response.detail || !!response.error"
    message: "return response.error || (typeof response.detail === 'string' ? response.detail : JSON.stringify(response.detail))"

  # A 300-page memorandum on CPU is minutes, not seconds: 3s × 400 is 20 minutes of patience.
  poll:
    url: "return scope.engineUrl + '/documents/jobs/' + response.id"
    until: "return response.status === 'COMPLETED'"
    failed: "return response.status === 'FAILED'"
    message: "return response.error || ('parse ' + response.status)"
    intervalMs: 3000
    maxAttempts: 400
files.config.yaml:
configSchema:
  type: object
  required: [fileUrl]
  properties:
    fileUrl:
      type: string
      title: File URL
      description: >-
        A URL the service can fetch the file from, usually a presigned link wired from an upstream
        file node, e.g. return signal.file.downloadUrl
      default: ""
      "ui:field": template
    fileName:
      type: string
      title: File Name
      description: >-
        The name with its extension, e.g. memorandum.pdf. The kind is read from the bytes, the name
        is for the filename dates and a better title.
      default: ""
      "ui:field": template
    includeFigures:
      type: boolean
      title: Include figures
      description: Render every figure as a PNG into the reply. Off for a text-and-tables read, which is smaller and faster.
      default: true
    ocr:
      type: boolean
      title: OCR scanned pages
      description: Run OCR on pages with no text layer. Off to read only what the file already says.
      default: true
"ui:order": [fileUrl, fileName, includeFigures, ocr]

files.node.yaml:
type: ParseDocument
kind: PromiseNode

name: Parse Document
category: Documents
color: "#0F766E"
logoUrl: https://res.cloudinary.com/sonik/image/upload/v1751366180/gravity/icons/gravityIcon.png

description: >-
  Read a file into its structure. Text in order, tables as rows, figures, lists, dates, and
  where each sits on the page

# Outcome first, disqualify by PROPERTY, never name another node. The property that sets this
# parser apart is its OUTPUT SHAPE: one typed structure with tables as rows and provenance to the
# bounding box, rather than one markdown string.
whenToUse: >-
  Read a document you already hold into a structure a pipeline or an Agent can work with: the
  text in reading order, every table as header and rows with numbers and units parsed, every
  figure as an image with its caption, every ordered list with its steps, the dates the document
  carries and where it was found, and for each of those the page and box it came from. Best when
  something downstream needs the TABLES or the FIGURES as things of their own rather than prose,
  or needs to point back at the exact place a figure came from. It only reads a file that already
  exists, on the platform's own service, and never sends the file to a third party.

auth:
  required: false

capabilities:
  # Parsing is deterministic for a file, so cache by CONTENT identity, never by URL: a presigned
  # link is a new signature every run over the same bytes. The etag an upstream file node delivers
  # is the identity; with none, the run is not cached.
  #
  # AND FOR A GIVEN FILE IT IS THE SERVICE'S CODE THAT DECIDES (2026-09-21). Keyed on the etag
  # alone, this node answers the same way for ever: the file has not changed, so the memory
  # stands, whatever the parser now does. Measured the day it was found: the parser was fixed so
  # that a table is not named after a date, the service was reloaded, the row was correctly read
  # again, and every document came back with the old names because the parse itself was replayed
  # from a trace. The run was clean and the fix reached nothing.
  #
  # `answeredBy` was built for exactly this a day earlier and three of this package's four nodes
  # declare it. This one, which is the node that parses, was missed.
  cacheable:
    ignore: [fileUrl]
    key: [etag]
    answeredBy: documents
files.test.yaml:
# Runs against the platform's own document service (npm run dev starts it beside umap), reading
# a ONE-PAGE public PDF, so it proves the whole chain: the job starts through the engine, is
# polled to COMPLETED, and the structure comes back. Shape assertions only, never exact words.
testData:
  config:
    fileUrl: https://www.w3.org/WAI/ER/tests/xhtml/testfiles/resources/pdf/dummy.pdf
    fileName: dummy.pdf
    includeFigures: false
  inputs:
    file:
      downloadUrl: https://www.w3.org/WAI/ER/tests/xhtml/testfiles/resources/pdf/dummy.pdf
      etag: dummy-pdf-etag
  expect:
    document: "return output.document.kind === 'pdf' && output.document.pages >= 1 && typeof output.document.content_hash === 'string'"
    text: "return typeof output.text === 'string' && output.text.length > 0"
    tables: "return Array.isArray(output.tables)"
    figures: "return Array.isArray(output.figures)"
    lists: "return Array.isArray(output.lists)"
    firstPages: "return typeof output.firstPages === 'string' && output.firstPages.length > 0"
    outline: "return Array.isArray(output.outline)"
    parts: "return Array.isArray(output.parts.tables) && Array.isArray(output.parts.figures)"
    files: "return output.files.some(f => f.name === 'text.md') && output.files.some(f => f.name === 'structure.json') && output.files.every(f => typeof f.text === 'string' || typeof f.base64 === 'string')"
